The test image shows a corn stalk with a dark brown/black lesion at the node/leaf collar area. The stalk is otherwise green. There appears to be debris at the leaf collar. This is a **stem** disease.

Stem candidates: Anthracnose, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Common_Smut, Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Head_Smut, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Purple_Leaf_Sheath, Stewart_S_Disease.

Top candidates based on symptoms: **Purple_Leaf_Sheath** (dark lesions at collar with tassel debris), **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot** (black nodes), **Anthracnose** (dark stalk lesions). Let me check references one at a time.
Purple_Leaf_Sheath shows discrete dark brown/purple lesions scattered on the stalk. The test image has a more concentrated dark area at the node. Let me check Physoderma_Stalk_Rot next.
Physoderma_Stalk_Rot shows scattered dark sporangia spots. The test image has a more solid dark lesion. Let me check Anthracnose stem reference.
Anthracnose stalk shows a dead/dry stalk with black lesions, not matching the green living stalk in the test. Let me check more candidates.
Diplodia Stalk Rot shows a dead, dry stalk that has broken over. Not matching. Let me check Charcoal Stalk Rot, Bacterial Stalk Rot, and Physoderma Brown Spot.
Charcoal Stalk Rot shows internal shredded pith with sclerotia. Not matching the external dark lesion on a green stalk. Let me check Bacterial Stalk Rot.
Not matching. Let me check Physoderma Brown Spot on stem.

This is very interesting. Physoderma Brown Spot on stem shows dark purplish-black spots on a green stalk near the node, with purple at the collar. This is visually similar to the test image. Let me use my last view to compare another Purple_Leaf_Sheath reference.

Now I can make my assessment. Comparing all references to the test image:

- **Test image**: Green living corn stalk with a concentrated dark brown/black lesion at the node/leaf collar junction, with visible debris at the collar area
- **Purple_Leaf_Sheath refs**: Dark brown/purple lesions on green stalks at collars. The KB states "pieces of tassel debris fallen into the leaf collar are present in almost all cases" - the test image clearly shows debris at the collar
- **Physoderma_Brown_Spot stem**: Similar dark spots near node but more scattered sporangia pattern
- **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot**: Scattered small dark spots, different pattern
- Other stalk rots (Anthracnose, Charcoal, Diplodia, Bacterial): All show dead/dry stalks or internal damage, not matching the green living stalk

The test image's key features (dark lesion at leaf collar on an otherwise green stalk, with visible debris trapped at the collar) most closely match Purple_Leaf_Sheath references and its diagnostic description.
